subject: Flexibility in specification of linear model of density?

messages.author: 3bfdefa58919d6ef
messages.subject: Flexibility in specification of linear model of density?
parts:
Hi All,

I'm wondering if it's possible in oSCR (and if so, how) to specify linear models of density that are more complex than just, for example:

D~cov*session 

For instance, what about a model where the interactions are specified by hand - such as when one has missing level combinations (i.e. interaction(factorA, factorB, drop=T).  I can see how to modify some of the source code (i.e. the model.matrix calls in oSCR.fit) to maybe make this happen, but I'm not sure if there is already an implemented approach I'm not catching.  Alternatively, it may be that missing level combinations are handled gracefully by nlm deeper in oSCR but I'm thinking that might not be the case.

THANKS,
Dan

--
--
Dan Barton

Best,

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [oscr] Re: Flexibility in specification of linear model of density?
parts:
hi Dan,
 I may not fully understand the full scope and complexity of your question but I do think if you can define the covariate explicitly (as an interaction or whatever) then you can just add it as a column to the state-space dataframe  -- so if you have the interaction(factorA, factorB, drop=T) and this implies some number of dummy variables or whatever, then you should be able to add those as columns to the ssDF , say called var1, var2, var3...., varN  and then model D ~ var1 + var2 + ....

 That should work fine, for any variable that you can define explicitly, and without having to rely on general R model specification formula conventions.
regards
andy
